title: Explicit spherical KK overlap and heavy-mode matching audit

secured_results.homogeneous_cubic_selection_rule: for W3=1, C_00n=0 for every n>0 by orthogonality
secured_results.direct_quartic: for W4=1, C_0000=1/(4pi), so cubic orthogonality does not remove a direct quartic operator
secured_results.profile_breaking: a Legendre component P_L in W3 activates the corresponding C_00L
secured_results.condition_audit: the norm matrix is diagnosed with lambda_min, lambda_max, kappa and lambda_min/lambda_max rather than an absolute Cholesky pivot alone

p2_breaking_example.interpretation: small internal inhomogeneity activates a calculable heavy-mode exchange contribution

protected_example.interpretation: the reduced scalar benchmark passes only because both the cubic selection rule and an assumed symmetry-forbidden direct quartic are imposed

robustness.safety_factor_10: the conditional M6-scale window of version 0.8 disappears for a one-decade cutoff separation at the default M6

limitations: the reduced matching indicator is not a complete dimensionful 4D Wilson coefficient
only axisymmetric scalar Legendre modes on the round S2 are included
metric, flux, radion, cap and brane-bending exchanges are omitted
the cubic and quartic parent vertices are benchmark inputs rather than derived from COS-02.2B
a vanishing direct quartic requires an explicit symmetry or topological selection rule
no evidence effect; K1-D and K1-E remain closed
